app.name: Gmail
app.description: Gmail is a popular email service provided by Google that offers a comprehensive REST API for integration.

notes: Tested: a custom auth config created without `oauth_redirect_uri` sends `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add`. Register exactly the URI your auth config sends, or set `oauth_redirect_uri` to `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback` and register that instead.
By default, Composio uses its own shared OAuth app, which displays 'Composio' on the consent screen.
Adding extra unverified scopes beyond Composio defaults will trigger Google's 'App is blocked' warning.
Ensure the Gmail API is enabled in your own Google Cloud project when using custom credentials to avoid API errors.

assumption: An AI agent that reads, modifies, and sends emails in any user's Gmail account using Google OAuth credentials.

verdict.headline: Full production access requires passing Google's sensitive/restricted scope review and mandatory annual CASA security assessments.
verdict.summary: You can immediately register an app and test locally with up to 100 users, but production deployment without warning screens requires Google's verification. Because agent scopes like `mail.google.com` or `gmail.modify` are restricted, you must provide a detailed justification video and potentially pass a third-party CASA security assessment.

handsOnEffort.label: 2–4 hours
handsOnEffort.basis: Cloud console setup, redirect URI configuration, and screen/video recording for verification.

timeToFirstConnection.label: 15–30 min
timeToFirstConnection.basis: Instant self-serve Google Cloud Console project creation and testing in Development mode.

timeToProduction.label: 2–10 weeks
timeToProduction.basis: Official review takes 3–10 business days, but real-world community reports cite 8–10 weeks plus CASA testing time.

verdict.longestPole: Google OAuth restricted scope verification and third-party CASA security assessment queues.
verdict.costDetail: Google OAuth verification is free, but an annual CASA security assessment by an authorized lab typically costs $500–$4,500 if mandated for restricted scopes.

easierPaths.condition: Limit scopes to basic profile and email data
easierPaths.effect: Avoids sensitive/restricted scope verification workflows entirely.

easierPaths.condition: Keep app in Testing mode (≤100 test users)
easierPaths.effect: Allows immediate production use for internal teams without verification, though refresh tokens expire after 7 days.

factors.detail: Developers can instantly create a project, configure consent screens, and set up OAuth credentials in the Google Cloud Console.
External apps requesting sensitive or restricted Gmail scopes must submit for Google OAuth verification to remove warning screens.
Brand verification requires domain ownership validation in Search Console, a privacy policy, and developer identity confirmation.
Restricted scopes storing or transmitting user data via third-party servers require an annual CASA security assessment by an authorized lab.
Standard Gmail API usage and OAuth access are free, with planned billing for threshold-exceeding usage starting late 2026.
No special partner program or sales contract is required to submit an app for verification.
Unverified apps in Testing mode are capped at 100 test users, and refresh tokens expire after 7 days.
Standard multi-tenant OAuth flow handles end-user connections once the primary client is verified.

phases.title: Project Creation and Setup
phases.outcome: A Google Cloud Project with the Gmail API enabled and configured consent screen.

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud Project
steps.details: Go to the [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com), click the project dropdown at the top, and click **New Project**. Enter a project name and click **Create**.
steps.agentAssist: Can generate project naming conventions and organizational guidelines.

steps.title: Enable the Gmail API
steps.details: Navigate to **APIs & Services → Library**, search for `Gmail API`, and click **Enable**.
steps.agentAssist: Can provide direct deep links or verify API availability status.

phases.title: Configure OAuth Consent Screen
phases.outcome: An OAuth consent screen configured with required app branding and scopes.

steps.title: Configure Consent Screen Details
steps.details: Go to **APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen**. Select **External** (or Internal if restricted to Workspace organization), fill in App name, User support email, and Developer contact information.
steps.agentAssist: Can draft all application descriptions, privacy policy text, and support email structures.

steps.title: Add Scopes
steps.details: Under **Scopes**, click **Add or Remove Scopes**, and select the required scopes such as `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly`, `gmail.modify`, `gmail.send`, and `mail.google.com`.
steps.agentAssist: Can list exact scope strings required for specific agent workflows.

phases.title: Create OAuth Client Credentials
phases.outcome: OAuth client ID and client secret generated for application authentication.

steps.title: Create OAuth Client ID
steps.details: Go to **APIs & Services → Credentials**, click **Create Credentials**, and select **OAuth client ID**. Choose **Web application** as the application type.
steps.agentAssist: Can document step-by-step instructions for selecting the correct credential type.

steps.title: Add Authorized Redirect URIs
steps.details: Under **Authorized redirect URIs**, add Composio's redirect URI: `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add` (or your custom callback URI). Click **Save** and copy your Client ID and Client Secret.
steps.agentAssist: Can format and validate redirect URI strings for configuration.

phases.title: Test with Own Account
phases.outcome: Verified local connection in testing mode with up to 100 test users.

steps.title: Add Test Users
steps.details: In **APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen**, scroll down to **Test users** and add your personal or team Google account emails. This allows testing before public verification.
steps.agentAssist: Can list team email addresses required for test user inclusion.

steps.title: Initiate Test Connection
steps.details: Trigger the OAuth flow via Composio or your local client. Note that unverified apps will display a prominent full-page warning screen ('Access blocked: App hasn't been verified') which you must bypass via Advanced links during testing.
steps.agentAssist: Can generate test scripts to initiate the OAuth flow against endpoints.

phases.title: Prepare for Review and Submit
phases.outcome: Submitted verification request for sensitive/restricted Gmail scopes.

steps.title: Record YouTube Demo Video
steps.details: Record an unlisted YouTube video showing the client ID, the consent screen with your app name, the complete OAuth sign-in flow, scope permission dialog, and how your application handles user data.
steps.agentAssist: Can write the complete script and shot list for the required verification video.

steps.title: Submit for Google OAuth Verification
steps.details: Go to **APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen** and click **Publish App** or **Submit for Verification**. Provide detailed justifications for each sensitive and restricted scope.
steps.agentAssist: Can draft comprehensive, policy-compliant scope justifications for `mail.google.com` and other agent scopes.

steps.title: Gmail reviews the submission
steps.details: Nothing to do but wait and watch for reviewer questions. The wait is 3–10 business days.
steps.agentAssist: An agent can watch the review inbox and draft replies to reviewer questions.

phases.title: Go live in Composio
phases.outcome: Gmail integration fully wired and operational via Composio with your custom credentials.

steps.title: Create Custom Auth Config in Composio
steps.details: Use Composio's CLI or API to create a custom auth config for `gmail`, providing your Google Client ID and Client Secret.
steps.agentAssist: Can generate the exact API payload or CLI command to register the custom auth config with Composio.

steps.title: Pass Auth Config ID in Tool Execution
steps.details: Reference your custom auth config ID when initiating tool connections or executing actions via the Composio SDK.
steps.agentAssist: Can integrate the auth config ID into your agent's execution runtime code.

requirements.detail: Create a project in the Google Cloud Console to house OAuth credentials and enable the Gmail API.
Configure callback URLs such as Composio's default URI (https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add) in the console.
Host a public privacy policy and verify domain ownership via Google Search Console for brand verification.
Provide a screen recording showing the end-to-end OAuth consent flow, requested scopes, and how user data is handled.
Complete an annual third-party security assessment via the CASA framework if handling restricted scope data on third-party servers.

scopes.purpose: Read all resources and metadata for user's email messages.
scopes.note: Common agent scope for reading emails
Common agent scope for managing labels and messages
Common agent scope for sending emails

scopes.purpose: Read email headers, labels, and metadata without message body access.
Full access to read, send, delete, and manage email messages.
scopes.note: Default full-access scope requested by Composio toolkit

blockers.title: App is blocked warning screen
blockers.symptom: Users see 'Access blocked: App hasn't been verified' when attempting to connect.
blockers.howToProceed: During testing, click 'Advanced' and then 'Go to app (unsafe)'. For production use, submit your app for Google OAuth verification.

blockers.title: Gmail API has not been used in project error
blockers.symptom: API calls fail with an error stating the Gmail API has not been used in the project.
blockers.howToProceed: Enable the Gmail API in Google Cloud Console under APIs & Services, wait a few minutes for propagation, and retry.

blockers.title: Error 400: invalid_scope
blockers.symptom: Authentication URL returns an invalid scope error.
blockers.howToProceed: Verify your scope values against Google's official scope documentation and ensure proper URL encoding.

blockers.title: CASA Security Assessment Requirement
blockers.symptom: Google requests a third-party security audit for restricted scopes.
blockers.howToProceed: Complete an annual security assessment via an authorized CASA lab, costing $500–$4,500 and taking 2–6 weeks.

nuances.title: Refresh Token Expiry in Testing Mode
nuances.detail: For apps in 'Testing' mode, refresh tokens expire automatically after 7 days, requiring re-authentication.

nuances.title: Restricted Scope Security Requirements
nuances.detail: Scopes like `mail.google.com` or `gmail.modify` are restricted and may trigger mandatory annual CASA security assessments.

nuances.title: Gmail API Quotas and Rate Limits
nuances.detail: Standard free usage allows 1,200,000 quota units per minute per project, 6,000 quota units per minute per user per project, and 80,000,000 daily quota units.

nuances.title: Verification Timelines Discrepancy
nuances.detail: Officially, reviews take 3–10 business days, but community reports frequently cite 8–10 weeks if requests stall or lack proper documentation.

steps: Create a custom OAuth app in Google Cloud Console with redirect URI `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add`.
Obtain your Google OAuth Client ID and Client Secret.
Register your custom credentials with Composio using the CLI or API auth config creation endpoint.
Pass your custom auth config ID when initiating user connections in Composio.
